proxy_language: Proto-Yeniseian (with Ket as the attested descendant) as primary proxy; Proto-Tungusic/Even-Evenki and Yukaghir as secondary regional comparanda
proxy_rationale: The Dyuktai culture (c. 35,000-10,000 BP, Aldan basin, Yakutia; bearers of microblade/wedge-shaped core technology ancestral to Beringian and some Native American populations) predates any language attested or reconstructable by the comparative method (time depth limit ~8-10 kya). No language can be tied to it demonstrably. The least indefensible proxy is Yeniseian (Ket, Kott, Yugh; reconstructed Proto-Yeniseian) because it is the sole surviving family in Central Siberia with deep, non-Altaic, non-Uralic roots and Ket hydronymy covers a wide area, plus Dene-Yeniseian hypothesis links it to Na-Dene (contested). Yukaghir (Kolyma/Tundra Yukaghir, Uralic-connected possibly) is the other candidate for Yakutia-Kolyma aboriginal language; Turkic Sakha and Tungusic are late arrivals (<1500 years) and should be avoided. Linkage is archaeologically motivated only; names are evocative, not claims of actual Dyuktai speech.
phonology: Ket (Vajda 2004; Georg 2007): consonants p b t d k q (uvular) g? s h x(velar fricative) ts, tʃ-like affricates, m n ŋ, l, j, w; ɬ marginal. Vowels i e a o u plus central ɨ/ə; five tone-like pitch contours in Ket (falling, rising, glottalization/laryngealization), represented in Latin transcriptions with diacritics or digits. Proto-Yeniseian reconstruction (Starostin, Vajda) has a voicing/aspiration-ish contrast in stops, uvular q, and glottalized elements. Reconstructed forms are tentative.
phonotactics: Mostly (C)V(C) syllables; monosyllabic and disyllabic roots dominate (Ket noun roots typically CV(C) or CVC). Onset clusters absent or very limited in roots; codas restricted to simple consonants (n, t, k, s, l, ŋ, m). Words rarely end in voiced stops. Verb complex is large but nouns are short. Recommended game shape: CV, CVC, CVCV, CVCVC with no clusters except across syllable boundary (-ŋ-, -nt-, -lk-).
orthography: Use simplified Latin Ket-style transliteration: p b t d k q g s x h m n ŋ l r? (avoid r word-initially) j w; affricates written ts and ch; vowels a e i o u and ɨ approximated as y; diacritics avoided. Digraphs: ts, ch, ng (for ŋ), kh (for x). Apostrophe may mark glottalization (e.g. k'). Hyphen separates morphemes or head-modifier in compounds.
morphology: Ket nouns have three genders (masculine, feminine, inanimate/neuter) marked on agreement not on the noun; plural suffixes -n, -ŋ, -aŋ, -naŋ, -ŋa (variable); possessive and case suffixes: locative -da/-ga, ablative -ka? , dative-like -ta, instrumental -ʔn? (details approximate). Verbs are polysynthetic with prefix chains. For naming purposes use bare noun roots, optionally with plural/collective -n or -ŋ, or a locative -da/-ga for places.
compounding: Ket forms compounds by juxtaposition of noun roots, modifier before head (N-N), e.g. possessor + possessed: kɨt (dog) + tul? type compounds; heads are final. Genitive/possessive relation shown by possessor noun preceding possessed noun, often with a possessive prefix on the head or simple juxtaposition. Agentive 'X-maker' formed by deverbal nominalizer on a verb root after object noun (approximate: object + verb-root-nominalized). Game recommendation: Modifier-Head order, joined with hyphen, e.g. qaʔ-tul.
noun_phrase_order: Modifier-head: possessor/adjective/attributive noun precedes head noun; numerals and demonstratives precede. Adjectives are largely stative verbs or nouns in attributive position.
sources: Vajda, Edward. 2004. Ket. Languages of the World/Materials 204. Lincom Europa.
Georg, Stefan. 2007. A Descriptive Grammar of Ket (Yenisei-Ostyak). Global Oriental.
Starostin, Sergei. Yeniseian etymological database (Starling database, starling.rinet.ru).
Vajda, Edward and Werner, Heinrich. Proto-Yeniseian reconstructions (Dene-Yeniseian work).
Mochanov, Yuri. 1977. Drevneyshie etapy zaseleniya chelovekom Severo-Vostochnoy Azii (Dyuktai culture archaeology).
notes: The Dyuktai culture has no linguistic attestation; any proxy is speculative. Yeniseian is used only for plausibility of Siberian phonotactics (short CV(C) roots, modifier-head compounds), not as a historical claim. Reconstructed Proto-Yeniseian forms listed are approximate and should be treated as sound-shape models rather than precise etyma. Avoid words identical to Sakha (Turkic), Evenki (Tungusic) or Russian items. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word since this culture is not Goidelic.
